issues.legal_issue: A later dismissal of a partition suit for nonpayment of a commissioner’s fee does not extinguish a preliminary decree already passed in terms of an award.
material_facts: A court passed a preliminary decree in terms of arbitrators’ award and appointed a commissioner to partition the property.
The suit was later dismissed because the commissioner’s fee was not paid.
The shares were demarcated and the family branches thereafter possessed their allotted properties separately.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal did not wipe out the preliminary decree.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that dismissal of the suit after a preliminary decree had been passed did not nullify that decree. It relied on the decree and the subsequent implementation of the partition; no statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this conclusion.

predicates.partition_suit_appeal: The matter is an appeal arising from a claim to partition family property.
predicates.preliminary_decree_entered: A court entered a preliminary decree in the partition proceeding.
predicates.original_suit_later_dismissed_for_unpaid: The original suit was later dismissed because a commissioner’s fee was not paid.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a partition claim involves a preliminary decree followed by dismissal of the original suit for nonpayment of a commissioner’s fee, the preliminary decree remains effective.

issues.legal_issue: An implemented division of family property, followed by separate possession and dealings with allotted shares, establishes severance of joint family status and defeats a later partition claim based on continued jointness.
material_facts: The family branches agreed to shares under an award, and a preliminary decree was passed in those terms.
A commissioner demarcated the shares, and the branches possessed their respective allotments separately thereafter.
Family members sold, mortgaged, exchanged, and collected rents or profits from property as their own; the properties were also recorded in their names.
The plaintiffs nevertheless sought partition on the basis that the properties remained jointly owned.
issues.conclusion: The family had been divided and its joint status had been severed; the later claim for partition on the basis of continued jointness could not succeed.
issues.legal_principle: The court treated the award’s implementation, separate possession, revenue entries, and dealings with allotted property as establishing severance. The zamindar’s treatment of the branches as joint holders did not alter their relationship inter se. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.

rule.if: partition_suit_appeal and prior_partition_implemented and branches_separately_possessed_allotted_shares and parties_dealt_with_shares_as_own

predicates.partition_suit_appeal: The matter is an appeal arising from a claim to partition family property.
predicates.prior_partition_implemented: A prior division of the family property was carried out.
predicates.branches_separately_possessed_allotted_s: The family branches separately possessed the shares allotted to them.
predicates.parties_dealt_with_shares_as_own: Family members dealt with property in their possession as their own, including by transferring or mortgaging it or collecting its income.

issues.definition: When a partition appeal involves an implemented prior division, separate possession of allotted shares, and dealings with those shares as individual property, the family’s joint status is severed.

issues.legal_issue: A party’s denial of service does not defeat a decree when the decree was entered against that party and the party later acted on the award and took possession under it.
material_facts: A party contended that he had not been served in the earlier partition suit.
The record of that suit had been destroyed.
A preliminary decree had been entered in terms of the award, and the party later took possession of property pursuant to the award and acted on it as effective.
issues.conclusion: The court inferred that the party had been duly served and rejected the contention that the decree was not binding on him.
issues.legal_principle: The court considered it reasonable to infer that a decree binding a person would not have been made unless that person had been served. The person’s subsequent conduct in taking possession under and acting on the award supported the inference. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.

rule.if: partition_suit_appeal and party_claimed_not_served and decree_entered_against_party and party_acted_under_award

predicates.partition_suit_appeal: The matter is an appeal arising from a claim to partition family property.
predicates.party_claimed_not_served: A party contended that the party had not been served in the earlier proceeding.
predicates.decree_entered_against_party: A court entered a decree affecting the party.
predicates.party_acted_under_award: The party later took possession or otherwise acted pursuant to the award on which the decree was based.

issues.definition: When a party in a partition appeal denies service but a decree was entered against that party and the party later acted under the award, service is inferred and the decree binds the party.

issues.legal_issue: A party who agreed to a partition award and allowed it to be implemented cannot, after a long delay, challenge the award as improperly granting another party a larger share.
material_facts: The parties agreed to the division under which the branches received different shares.
The award was implemented, and the branches remained in separate possession of their allotted properties.
The challenge to the share granted to one branch was raised decades after the award had been acted upon.
issues.conclusion: It was not open to the party to challenge the award on the ground that the arbitrators had improperly granted a larger share.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that, after the parties agreed to the award and its terms were carried out, a party could not raise an impropriety challenge decades later. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.

rule.if: partition_suit_appeal and parties_agreed_to_award and award_fully_implemented and challenge_raised_after_long_delay

predicates.partition_suit_appeal: The matter is an appeal arising from a claim to partition family property.
predicates.parties_agreed_to_award: The parties agreed to the terms of the partition award.
predicates.award_fully_implemented: The award was carried out and the parties took possession in accordance with it.
predicates.challenge_raised_after_long_delay: A party raised a challenge to the award only after a substantial period had passed.

issues.definition: When parties to a partition appeal agreed to an award, it was implemented, and a challenge was raised only after a long delay, the late challenge is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant cannot obtain the whole of a deceased family member’s share through an alleged adoption or adverse possession when the agreed award reserved that share for the widow’s lifetime and provided for its later division among the family branches.
material_facts: The award provided that the deceased member’s share would remain with his widow during her lifetime and would thereafter be divided among the three branches in the same proportions as the other family property.
A claimant asserted that a son had been adopted by the deceased and that the claimant had acquired the deceased’s share by adverse possession.
The court found no evidence supporting the adoption or adverse-possession claims.
issues.conclusion: The claimant’s claim to the deceased member’s share on the grounds of adoption and adverse possession failed; the share was to be dealt with according to the award.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the terms of the agreed award, which reserved the share for the widow’s lifetime and directed its later division among the branches. It also held that the deceased could not make a will of his undivided share and that the asserted adoption and adverse possession were unsupported by evidence. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.

rule.if: partition_suit_appeal and award_reserved_share_for_widow_then_branch_allocation and (claim_based_on_adoption or claim_based_on_adverse_possession) and no_evidence_supports_claim

predicates.partition_suit_appeal: The matter is an appeal arising from a claim to partition family property.
predicates.award_reserved_share_for_widow_then_bran: The award gave a deceased member’s share to the widow for her lifetime and provided for its later allocation among family branches.
predicates.claim_based_on_adoption: The claimant relied on an asserted adoption as a basis for claiming the deceased member’s share.
predicates.claim_based_on_adverse_possession: The claimant relied on adverse possession as a basis for claiming the deceased member’s share.
predicates.no_evidence_supports_claim: The evidence did not support the asserted adoption or adverse possession.

issues.definition: When a partition appeal concerns a share reserved for a widow and later allocation among family branches, a claim to the entire share based on adoption or adverse possession fails if the evidence does not support that basis.
